unit.title: Perform submerged arc welding to AWS specification

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A specification says the flange-to-web welds of a bridge girder are to be made by submerged arc welding (SAW) "to the AWS structural code the Centre uses". Which document must the operator work from?
options: The wire supplier's price list for the job
The client's purchase order
The label on the flux bag
A SAW WPS that covers the joint

questions.stem: Under many AWS structural codes, SAW procedures can be "prequalified". What does this mean for the shop?
options: No written WPS of any kind is needed for the job
A WPS within the code limits needs no PQR test
Any operator may weld it without a test
The welds need no inspection after welding

questions.stem: In AWS terms, the person who sets up and runs a SAW tractor is qualified as what?
options: A welding operator
A welder
A welding inspector
A fitter

questions.stem: Why must a SAW welding operator pass a test, even though the machine moves the arc along the joint?
options: Only so that he can be paid at a higher rate
Because SAW is only ever used on pipe
His set-up and control decide the weld
Because the code bans automatic welding

questions.stem: A SAW WPS was qualified with a single wire. The shop now wants to add a second wire behind the first (tandem). What is needed?
options: A WPS qualified for two wires
Nothing, since it is still the SAW process
Only a larger flux hopper
Only a faster travel speed

questions.stem: In the wire-flux class F7A2-EM12K, what does the 7 mainly tell you?
options: The flux grain size
The wire diameter in mm
The number of passes allowed
Minimum tensile strength

questions.stem: The 2 in F7A2-EM12K comes straight after the A. What does it relate to?
options: The wire is 2 mm across
Two passes at most are allowed
The impact test temperature
The flux holds 2% moisture

questions.stem: The SAW wire class EM12K has an M straight after the E. What does that M show?
options: Metal-cored wire
Medium manganese content
Mixed gas shielding
Made for multi-pass work

questions.stem: What is an "active" SAW flux?
options: A flux that gives off shielding gas only
A flux that adds Mn and Si to the weld
A flux that must be kept hot in the hopper
A flux that can be used only once

questions.stem: With an active flux, why must the arc voltage be held within the WPS range, especially on multi-pass welds?
options: Higher voltage melts more flux and adds more alloy
Higher voltage turns all of the flux into gas
Lower voltage makes the slag stick hard to the plate
Voltage has no effect with an active flux

questions.stem: Why might a WPS for a thick multi-pass SAW joint call for a "neutral" flux?
options: It needs no drying before use at all
It works only on an AC supply
It makes the slag easier to see
It keeps the weld chemistry steady

questions.stem: A SAW job must pass impact (toughness) tests. Why does the WPS limit the heat input?
options: High heat input wastes a lot of flux
High heat input makes the bead far too narrow to pass
High heat input can make the weld and HAZ less tough
High heat input stops the slag peeling off

questions.stem: What does a Charpy V-notch impact test show about a SAW weld?
options: How hard the surface of the cap is
How much flux was burned in the pass
The energy to break a notched piece at a set temperature
How many minutes the arc was running

questions.stem: Charpy pieces from a SAW procedure test are notched in the weld metal and also in the heat-affected zone (HAZ). Why the HAZ too?
options: The HAZ is the easiest place to cut
Heat from the weld can change its toughness
The code wants the notch away from the weld
The HAZ never contains any faults

questions.stem: For a SAW groove weld procedure test on thick plate, which set of tests is usual?
options: A paint test and a leak test
A hardness test on the cap, and nothing else
A fillet break and a nick-break test
Tensile, side bend and any impact tests

questions.stem: In an all-weld-metal tension test, where is the test bar taken from?
options: Entirely from the weld metal
Across the weld and both plates
From the plate only, away from the weld
From the run-off tab only

questions.stem: A double-sided SAW butt must have complete joint penetration. After the first side is welded, what is usually done before the second side?
options: Weld the second side at once, with more current
Back gouge or grind to sound metal
Paint the root side to seal it
Nothing, as SAW always fully penetrates

questions.stem: After a structural butt seam is welded with SAW, what is usually done with the run-on and run-off tabs?
options: They are left on to strengthen the seam ends
They are painted to match the plate
They are bent over and hammered flat
They are cut off and the ends ground smooth

questions.stem: Why must run-on and run-off tabs be of the same kind of steel and thickness as the job?
options: So the weld at the ends matches the job
So the tabs can be sold later for scrap
So the flux sticks to them better
So the inspector can stamp them

questions.stem: A prequalified SAW joint detail gives a root face and root gap with tolerances. The fit-up is outside them. What should happen?
options: Weld it, and add a pass to make up
Weld it, then X-ray it to check
Correct the fit-up, or qualify the joint by test
Change to a larger wire size

questions.stem: On a pressure vessel job, why are the flux batch and wire heat numbers written on the weld record?
options: To work out the cost of the job
To claim back money for the empty bags
So each weld traces to certified consumables
So the storeman knows where each bag is stacked

questions.stem: A delivery of SAW wire and flux arrives for a code job. What should be checked first?
options: That classes and batches match the certificates
That the bags are a colour the team likes best
That the price is lower than for the last order
That the wire looks shiny on the outside

questions.stem: A SAW PQR plate passes all its tests. The WPS later written from it gives a current range much wider than the code allows. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, as the range is up to the shop to choose
The PQR must be thrown away and redone
The welds will simply be stronger
The WPS must keep to the ranges the code allows

questions.stem: A macro etch is cut from a SAW flange-to-web fillet weld. What should it show?
options: The type of flux that was used
Fusion to the root and both parts, with legs to size
The arc voltage that was set
The operator's ID number

questions.stem: Why might a SAW procedure test on high-strength steel include hardness tests across the HAZ?
options: Hard zones in the HAZ can crack in service
Hardness shows the flux's grain size
Hardness tells the arc voltage used
Hardness is the only test that the code allows

questions.stem: A radiograph finds slag in a SAW seam. The shop repairs it by gouging out and re-welding with MMAW. What must cover the repair?
options: Nothing, as repairs are not welds
A WPS for the repair process
The original SAW WPS only
The flux maker's leaflet

questions.stem: A specification calls for "spot radiography" of SAW tank seams. What does this mean?
options: Every seam is X-rayed along its full length
Only welds with visible spots are X-rayed
Set lengths at chosen places are X-rayed
Only the run-off tabs are X-rayed

questions.stem: The SAW travel speed dial reads 500 mm/min. How should the recorder check the real speed for a PQR?
options: Trust the dial on the controller
Ask the operator what he thinks
Count the flux bags used during the run
Time the head over a measured length

questions.stem: Three Charpy pieces break at 40 J, 34 J and 31 J. The specification needs an average of at least 27 J. What is the average, and does it pass?
options: 31 J, fail
35 J, fail
105 J, pass
35 J, pass

questions.stem: A tensile bar is 20 mm × 25 mm in cross-section and breaks at 245 kN. What is its tensile strength?
options: 490 MPa
49 MPa
245 MPa
980 MPa

questions.stem: A specification needs weld metal of at least 480 MPa tensile strength. The test gives 520 MPa. Does it pass, and by how much?
options: No, it is 40 MPa short
Yes, by 40 MPa
Yes, by 520 MPa
No, it is 520 MPa short

questions.stem: A PQR test uses 2 plates, each 500 mm × 150 mm × 25 mm. Steel weighs 7 850 kg per m³. About what do the two plates weigh together?
options: About 15 kg
About 3 kg
About 29 kg
About 59 kg

questions.stem: The two PQR plates weigh about 29 kg together. How should they be moved to the welding table?
options: With a hoist, or a two-person lift with gloves and boots
By one person, holding them against the chest
By sliding them off the bench onto the floor
By dragging them with a wire rope by hand

questions.stem: SAW runs at high current for long periods. What must be checked on the welding cables?
options: That they are brightly coloured
That they are as long as possible
That they are coiled up tightly on the floor
That they are rated for the current and duty

questions.stem: A SAW run on the inside of a large tank shell needs the operator to be inside the tank. What must be in place?
options: Only a torch and a radio
A fan that blows flux dust in
A confined space permit, air supply and a standby person
A longer welding cable only

questions.stem: An operator turns the voltage up past the WPS range to make the bead wider on a seam. As team leader, what do you do?
options: Let him, as long as it looks good
Stop and bring it back inside the range
Record his value as the new WPS setting
Turn the travel speed up as well

questions.stem: A spot radiograph of a tank seam shows a fault. The specification says more spots must then be taken on that seam. Why?
options: To use up the spare X-ray film
To find out which operator welded the seam
To give the operator more practice
To find how far the fault runs in the seam

questions.stem: Which of these would you expect to find on a SAW WPS but not on an MMAW WPS?
options: The grade and thickness of the plate
The flux and wire-flux class
The design of the joint and its gap
The position the weld is made in

questions.stem: A SAW procedure was qualified on 25 mm plate. Can the WPS be used on 60 mm plate?
options: Only if 60 mm is inside the range the test covers
Yes, a SAW WPS covers any thickness
No, SAW can never weld 60 mm plate
Yes, if the current is doubled

questions.stem: Why may a SAW procedure test include a chemical analysis of the weld metal?
options: To find the operator's ID number
To check that the flux has not changed colour in store
The flux and settings can change its make-up
To find how much the plate weighs

questions.stem: Why does a SAW WPS for impact-tested work often set a maximum interpass temperature?
options: To save flux between each of the passes
So heat does not build up and lower toughness
So the slag peels off the seam much more easily
So the operator can rest between passes

questions.stem: Before SAW of a thick plate joint, why might the plate edges be checked by ultrasonic testing?
options: To check how thick the paint on the plate is
To measure the depth of the flux
To find the grade of the plate
To find layers in the plate that could open

questions.stem: On a double-V SAW joint in thick plate, why are passes laid on each side in turn?
options: To balance shrinkage and keep the plate flat
To use less flux on the job
To let the operator rest
So no back gouging is ever needed

questions.stem: A SAW WPS lists DCEP. The shop's power source has been reconnected for DCEN. What should happen before welding?
options: Weld anyway, as polarity does not matter in SAW
Turn the current up to make up for it
Set it back to DCEP, or qualify DCEN
Use less flux on the joint

questions.stem: Why are PQRs and welding operator records kept on file after the job is finished?
options: They can be sold to other shops
The client or inspector may ask later
They are needed to order more flux
They show the machine's serial number

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In the class F7A2-EM12K, what does the letter E tell you?
In the wire class EM12K, the 12 gives the usual amount of which element, in hundredths of a per cent?
What do the letters CJP stand for, for a groove weld that is fused through the full thickness of the joint?
What do the letters PJP stand for, for a groove weld that does not go through the full thickness?
Name the process that cuts a groove with a carbon electrode and a jet of compressed air, often used to back gouge a SAW root.
1 ksi is about 6.9 MPa. About how many MPa is 70 ksi, to the nearest 10?
What is the name for the person who watches a PQR test and signs that the values recorded are true?
A specification asks for 3 spot radiographs for every 15 m of seam. How many spots are needed for 60 m of seam?
Impact test energy is given in units with the symbol J. What is the name of the unit?
Name the heated cabinet where opened SAW flux is kept warm and dry before use, as the maker says.
What is the name for a hidden layer in thick steel plate, lying parallel to its surface, that can open when welded across?
Of 25 m of seam X-rayed, 0.5 m has faults that need repair. What percentage of the X-rayed length is that?
What is the full term for the distance from the end of the contact tip to the plate, which a SAW WPS sets?
What word does the code use for a joint detail and WPS it accepts without a procedure test, as long as all its limits are met?
What name is given to laying a layer of stainless or wear-resistant metal over carbon steel with SAW?

essays.stem: Explain each part of the SAW wire-flux class F7A2-EM12K, and how you would use it to choose and check consumables for a job that needs impact tests.
essays.modelAnswer: F shows it is a flux classification. The 7 shows the weld metal's minimum tensile strength, in units of 10 000 psi, so about 480 MPa. The A shows the weld metal was tested as-welded; a P would show it was tested after heat treatment. The 2 gives the temperature at which the weld metal passed its impact test, in the scale the standard uses (minus 20 °F, about minus 29 °C). After the dash, E shows a solid wire electrode, M shows medium manganese, 12 shows about 0.12% carbon, and K shows the wire is killed with silicon. For a job with impact tests, I check that the strength is at least what the drawing needs, that the A or P matches whether the job is heat treated, and that the impact temperature is as low as, or lower than, the job's. Then I check the delivered wire and flux are that class, with matching batch certificates, and that the WPS lists that combination.
markingPoints: F, 7 (tensile strength) and A/P explained
2 explained as the impact test temperature
E, M, 12 and K in the wire class explained
Matches strength, heat treatment and impact temperature to the job
Checks certificates, batches and the WPS

essays.stem: Compare active, neutral and alloy SAW fluxes, and explain why the type of flux matters for multi-pass welds and for the arc voltage.
essays.modelAnswer: An active flux adds manganese and silicon to the weld. This helps when welding over light rust or scale, and gives good resistance to porosity and cracking on one- or two-pass welds. But the amount added depends on how much flux is melted, which rises with arc voltage. On a thick multi-pass weld, each pass adds more, so the weld metal can become too strong and brittle and may crack. That is why voltage must stay inside the WPS range, and why active fluxes are often limited in the number of passes or the plate thickness. A neutral flux changes the weld chemistry very little, even if the voltage changes, so it suits thick multi-pass joints; the wire must then supply the deoxidisers. An alloy flux carries alloying elements on purpose, to make an alloy weld metal from a plain wire, for example for surfacing. For any flux, the type and class must be the one the WPS lists.
markingPoints: Active flux adds Mn and Si; good for one or two passes
Alloy pick-up rises with voltage; risk of brittle weld on many passes
Neutral flux changes chemistry little; suits multi-pass
Alloy flux adds alloy on purpose
Flux type must match the WPS

essays.stem: Explain how a SAW welding operator is qualified under the AWS code the Centre uses, how this differs from qualifying a manual welder, and how the qualification is kept in force.
essays.modelAnswer: A manual welder controls the arc by hand, so his test checks his hand skill in each position. A SAW welding operator runs a machine that moves the arc, so his test checks that he can set up and control the machine to make a sound weld. He welds a test plate to a qualified WPS, setting the stick-out, flux depth, wire position, current, voltage and travel speed, and tracking the joint. The test plate is inspected and tested, often by bend tests or radiography, as the code sets. His record shows the process, the type of equipment, such as single or multiple wires, and the range he is qualified for. Because SAW is mainly done flat, the position range is usually small. To keep it in force, the operator must use the process within the time the code allows, recorded in a continuity log. If his work shows a reason to doubt his skill, he can be retested.
markingPoints: Explains welder (hand skill) versus operator (machine control)
Operator welds a test plate to a qualified WPS
Test plate inspected and tested as the code sets
Record shows process, equipment type and range
Continuity of use and retest when in doubt

essays.stem: Describe how the test pieces from a SAW procedure test on thick plate are marked out, removed, prepared and tested, and how the results are judged.
essays.modelAnswer: First the whole plate is inspected by eye, and often by radiography or ultrasonic testing, before any cutting. The run-on and run-off ends are discarded. Using the code's layout, I mark where each test piece comes from: transverse tensile bars, side bend strips and, if the job needs them, Charpy pieces and a macro section. Each piece is numbered and stamped. The pieces are cut by saw or machine, not by flame close to the weld, and finished to the sizes the code gives, with edges rounded and marks running lengthwise. The tensile bars are pulled to failure and the strength compared with the minimum for the plate. The side bends are bent round the set former and checked for open faults bigger than the code allows. Charpy pieces are cooled to the test temperature and broken, and the average and lowest values are compared with the specification. The macro shows fusion and penetration. All results go on the PQR.
markingPoints: Inspects the plate before cutting and discards the ends
Marks out and identifies pieces using the code's layout
Cuts by saw or machine and prepares to size
Explains how tensile, side bend and Charpy results are judged
Records results on the PQR

essays.stem: Explain why heat input and interpass temperature are controlled on SAW work that must pass impact tests, and how you would monitor them on the job.
essays.modelAnswer: SAW can put a lot of heat into the joint because it runs at high current. If too much heat goes in, the weld metal and the heat-affected zone cool slowly and their grain grows coarse. Coarse grain is less tough, so the weld may fail the impact test or crack in cold or shock loading. If the plate is allowed to get very hot between passes, the same thing happens. So the WPS sets a maximum heat input and a maximum interpass temperature, and sometimes a minimum preheat. On the job, I check that current, voltage and travel speed stay within the WPS, and I work out the heat input from them, timing the travel over a measured length. Before each pass, I check the temperature beside the joint with a temperature crayon or contact thermometer, and wait if it is above the limit. I record the values on the weld record.
markingPoints: High heat gives slow cooling and coarse grain
Coarse grain lowers toughness and impact results
WPS limits heat input and interpass temperature
Checks volts, amps and measured travel speed and works out heat input
Checks interpass temperature before each pass and records it

essays.stem: Describe how a double-sided complete joint penetration SAW butt weld is made in thick plate, including the back gouging and the checks between the two sides.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the WPS for the joint design, wire, flux, settings and the order of passes. The plates are bevelled, cleaned and fitted with the root face and gap the WPS gives, and tacked. Run-on and run-off tabs of the same steel and thickness are fitted at each end. I weld the first side with the passes the WPS sets, cleaning the slag after each pass. Then the plate is turned over. The root is back gouged, by air carbon arc gouging or grinding, until sound weld metal from the first side is reached. I grind the gouged groove smooth and clean, and check it by eye, and with dye penetrant or magnetic particle testing if the WPS asks, to make sure no faults are left. The second side is then welded, laying passes on each side in turn where needed to balance distortion. Afterwards the tabs are removed and the ends ground, and the weld is inspected.
markingPoints: Prepares, fits and tacks to the WPS, with tabs
Welds the first side and cleans between passes
Back gouges to sound metal and grinds smooth
Checks the gouge before welding the second side
Welds the second side, balances distortion, removes tabs and inspects

essays.stem: Explain what a prequalified SAW WPS is, the conditions it must meet, and what the shop must still do before using it.
essays.modelAnswer: A prequalified WPS is one that the code accepts without a procedure test, because the code itself sets joint details and limits that are known to work. Under many AWS structural codes, SAW can be prequalified. To be prequalified, the WPS must use a joint detail from the code's list, with the root face, gap and angles within its tolerances. The base metal and the wire-flux combination must be ones the code lists for each other, and the settings, such as wire size, current, number of electrodes and pass size, must stay inside the code's limits. Preheat and interpass rules must also be met. The shop must still write the WPS down, check every value against the code, and have it approved. The operators must still be qualified, and the welds must still be inspected. If any condition cannot be met, the procedure must be qualified by a test and a PQR.
markingPoints: Defines prequalified: accepted without a procedure test
Joint detail and tolerances from the code
Listed base metal and wire-flux combination; settings within limits
WPS must still be written, checked and approved
Operators qualified and welds inspected; otherwise qualify by test

essays.stem: Spot radiography of a SAW tank seam finds slag inclusions in one film. Describe the steps that follow, up to the seam being accepted.
essays.modelAnswer: First the film is read by a qualified person against the code's limits, and the fault is confirmed as rejectable. It is marked on the seam using the film markers. The specification will usually call for extra spots on the same seam, on each side of the faulty one, to find how far the problem runs. If these show faults too, the whole seam may need to be X-rayed. I check the welding records for that seam to find the cause, such as poor slag removal between passes or a wire placed too close to one side wall. The faulty lengths are gouged or ground out to sound metal, checked, and re-welded to a WPS that covers the repair, by a qualified welder or operator. The repaired areas are X-rayed again. Only when all films are acceptable is the seam accepted. Every step, film number and repair is recorded, and the cause is used to stop it happening again.
markingPoints: Film read and fault confirmed against the code
Extra (tracer) spots taken to find the extent
Cause found from the records
Repair by gouging, checking and re-welding to a WPS
Re-radiograph, record and prevent recurrence

essays.stem: Explain how you would control SAW wire and flux on a pressure vessel job so that every weld can be traced to certified consumables.
essays.modelAnswer: When wire and flux arrive, I check that the class on each coil and bag matches the WPS and the order, and that a certificate comes with each batch, giving its test results. I record the batch and heat numbers in the store book and keep the certificates on file. I store flux sealed and dry, as the maker says, and keep different classes and batches apart and labelled. Wire coils stay in their wrapping until used. When consumables are issued to the operator, I record which batches went to which job. On the weld record, the operator writes the wire heat and flux batch for each seam. Recovered flux is kept with its own batch and not mixed with other classes. Any bag that is damaged, wet or unlabelled is set aside and not used. At the end, the records link every seam to its consumables and certificates, so the inspector or client can trace them.
markingPoints: Checks class and certificates on receipt and records batches
Stores sealed, dry and separated by class and batch
Records issue of batches to each job
Weld records show wire heat and flux batch per seam
Sets aside doubtful consumables; records allow full tracing

essays.stem: Explain the main inspection and testing methods used on finished SAW welds on a steel girder or tank, and what each can and cannot find.
essays.modelAnswer: Visual inspection is done on every weld. It finds surface faults such as undercut, poor bead shape, surface cracks, unfilled craters and wrong weld size, but cannot see inside. Dye penetrant testing finds fine cracks open to the surface on any metal, but nothing below it. Magnetic particle testing finds surface and just-below-surface cracks in carbon steel, but not deep faults. Radiography gives a picture of the inside of a butt weld and shows slag, porosity and incomplete penetration well, but may miss thin, flat faults such as lack of side-wall fusion unless the beam lines up with them, and it needs licensed people and a cleared area. Ultrasonic testing sends sound into the weld and is good at finding flat faults and lack of fusion in thick welds, but needs a skilled operator and is harder on fillet welds. The specification says which methods, how much and the acceptance limits.
markingPoints: Visual: surface faults and size only
Dye penetrant and magnetic particle: surface or near-surface only
Radiography: volume faults; may miss flat faults; licensed people
Ultrasonic: good for flat faults and thick welds; skilled operator
The specification sets methods, extent and limits

practical1.title: SAW procedure qualification test plate to a draft WPS, with a witnessed PQR record (fallback where the Centre has no SAW machine)
practical1.brief: The Centre may not have a submerged arc machine, so this task has two forms. The assessor tells the group which form it will do, and writes that on the result sheet. Form A (the Centre has a SAW machine): with the assessor's draft WPS for a double-sided butt joint in carbon steel plate (about 12–20 mm), the group checks the plates, wire and flux against their certificates, fits and tacks the plates, and fixes run-on and run-off tabs. Members share the roles of operator, flux and tracking, meters and timing, and witness/recorder, changing roles so that every member operates at least one pass and witnesses at least one pass. The group welds the first side, back gouges or grinds to sound metal, checks the gouge, and welds the second side, recording the real current, voltage, timed travel speed, stick-out and interpass temperature for every pass on the PQR sheet. Form B (no SAW machine): the group visits a fabrication shop that uses SAW, by arrangement and with the shop's permission, and witnesses and records the welding of a test plate by the shop's operator; or, if no visit is possible, the group welds the same double-sided joint with a gas-shielded flux-cored or MIG wire on a travel carriage, if the Centre has one, as a stand-in, and records it in the same way. Form B shows the planning, witnessing and recording skills only. The SAW operating skill must be assessed later on a SAW machine, and the assessor notes this. In both forms, each member signs the passes he or she witnessed. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Draft SAW WPS, blank PQR sheet and consumable check sheet (from the assessor)
Carbon steel plates bevelled to the WPS, with run-on and run-off tabs of the same steel and thickness
SAW wire and flux of the class on the WPS, with their batch certificates (Form A)
SAW tractor or head with track, flux hopper and a DC power source (Form A); or a travel carriage with a flux-cored or MIG set (Form B stand-in)
Checked clamp meter and voltmeter, stopwatch, steel rule, temperature crayons or contact thermometer
Grinder, or air carbon arc gouging set if the Centre allows it, chipping hammer and wire brush
Lifting gear or a hoist for the plates
photos: The plates, wire and flux laid out with their certificates and the check sheet
The fitted and tacked joint with the run-on and run-off tabs
The head (or carriage) set on the joint before the first pass, with the stick-out being measured
The back-gouged root after grinding, before the second side
The finished weld on both sides
The completed PQR sheet with every pass recorded and signed
checklist: Checked plate, wire and flux against the WPS and their certificates
Fitted and tacked the joint and fixed tabs as the WPS sets
Set up and ran a pass (Form A), or helped set up the stand-in or visit welding (Form B)
Measured current and voltage at the arc and timed the travel speed correctly
Checked the back gouge reached sound metal before the second side
Recorded real values for each pass and signed only what he or she witnessed
Worked safely, moving the heavy plates with lifting gear or a team lift
safety: Wear eye protection with a filter at all times near the head: the arc can flash through the flux
Hot slag can peel off in long strips: let it cool and handle it with tools and gloves
Use extraction when filling hoppers and handling flux; wear a dust mask if the SDS says
Move plates with a hoist or a team lift; keep hands clear of the tractor and track
On a shop visit, follow the host shop's rules and stay where the guide says; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Inspect, cut and test SAW weld samples, and judge them against the WPS and the specification in a test report
practical2.brief: The assessor provides SAW weld samples: a butt weld plate and a fillet weld (such as a flange-to-web section), made at the Centre or by a local fabricator, with a copy of the WPS and the acceptance limits from the specification. If no SAW samples can be got, the assessor provides thick multi-pass MMAW or FCAW samples as stand-ins and notes this on the result sheet. Share the work so every member has a named part: the group plans where test pieces come from and marks them out. Members inspect the samples by eye and with gauges, recording weld size, undercut and surface faults; cut the macro sections and side bend strips by saw (the assessor or a supervised member operates the saw); grind, polish and etch the macros; bend the side bend strips in the guided bend jig under supervision; and measure and record every result. The group then writes a test report that compares each result with the specification, says pass or fail with reasons, and, for any failure, gives the most likely cause and what should change in the procedure. checklist: Helped plan and mark out test pieces from the right places, discarding the ends

Wear eye protection when grinding; clamp the pieces
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
